title: Data and privacy
examples: What kind of personal information do social media apps collect?
How do cookies actually track my activity on a website?
What are my rights when a company wants to use my data?

explain.say: Some apps collect information about your location when you use them.
Cookies are small text files websites store on your device for remembering you.

draw.text: Cookies: small text files on your device.

explain.say: When you sign up for a service, you often give them personal identifiers like your name.
You have the right to know what data companies are collecting about you.
If you want to stop tracking, you can adjust your privacy settings on the app.

draw.text: Adjusting privacy settings helps control data.

explain.say: In real life, think about signing up for a new online game.

draw.text: Real life: New online game sign-up.

faq.a: A cookie is a small piece of data stored on your computer by a website. It helps the site remember your preferences when you visit again.

faq.q: Do all apps collect my location data?
faq.a: No, apps only collect location data if you give them permission to do so. You should always check those permissions.
asks: Do I have to allow location services?

faq.q: What does it mean that I have the right to erasure?
faq.a: It means you have the right to ask a company to permanently delete all the personal data they hold about you. They must comply with this request.
asks: Can I make companies forget me?
What is the right to be forgotten?

faq.q: If I delete my account, is all my data gone forever?
faq.a: While the company should delete it, sometimes they keep anonymized data for longer periods. You should read the privacy policy carefully.
asks: How long do companies keep my old info?

faq.q: If I use a VPN, does that stop all data collection?
faq.a: A VPN can hide your IP address, which is good, but it does not stop apps from collecting data you actively give them. It is one tool among many.
asks: Is a VPN a total privacy shield?
What is the best way to stop tracking?

facts: Apps can collect data such as your contacts, photos, and location.
Cookies are small files that websites use to track your activity across pages.
You have the right to access and request the deletion of your personal data.
Checking app permissions is the first step in protecting your privacy.

quiz.say: A website uses cookies to remember what items are in your shopping cart.
quiz.why: Cookies are designed to store small pieces of information on your device so websites can remember your choices.

wrong.0: The server stores data centrally, but cookies are stored locally on your device.
wrong.1: History is a record of pages visited; cookies are the small files that make the remembering happen.
wrong.2: Passwords are secret keys; cookies are much smaller, less sensitive tracking bits.

quiz.say: Which right allows you to ask a company to delete your saved information?
quiz.why: The right to erasure gives you control over the data a company holds about you.

wrong.0: This right only lets you see the data, not delete it.
wrong.1: This right lets you take your data somewhere else, but not necessarily delete it.
wrong.2: Consent is what you give permission for; it is not the action of deleting data.

quiz.say: If an app asks for your contacts list, what is the main privacy risk?

options.show: The app will cost more money
options.say: The app will cost more money

quiz.why: Your contacts list contains personal phone numbers and names that are private information.

wrong.0: This is a performance issue, not a direct risk to your personal data.
wrong.1: Data collection does not usually affect the price of the application.
wrong.3: This is a technical issue, not a privacy risk related to data collection.
